metadata.description: P4 — the prompty / prompter / pioneer / puppeteer meta-prompting framework; ships the Roboto four-lens reasoning instance and the standalone epistemic plugins (vlds, verification-discipline, emission-discipline, envelope-discipline) as installable plugins.

plugins.name: mister
plugins.description: Roboto / "The Init Elegance" — the four-lens reasoning instance of the P4 framework: identity, rubric, orchestration, vlds, templates, bias-patterns, isomorphic-operations, sjc-indexer, activation, and persistence skills, plus a roboto subagent and the four P4 gate commands. `p4.py` makes the closure model executable: it derives every closure from the skills' own `metadata.p4`, and reconciles the rubric gate table against that graph so the puppeteer→prompty registration loop is machine-checked at both ends.

plugins.name: vlds
plugins.description: VLDS — the P4 framework's epistemic discipline as a standalone, runtime dashboard of four instruments plus a conductor. The gate routes every load-bearing claim through VERIFIABLE → VERIFIED → CONFIRMED / PENDING / HEDGED — verify before you assert, state what you can't verify with its uncertainty attached. The guide loop disciplines the need behind the claim, configuring and recording the model's behavior as the user steers it. The inspector re-examines a high-stakes verdict through independent perspectives to corroborate, overturn, or surface it — the outside eye the others cannot be. The gc is a garbage collector for belief state — stored rules, memories, and training-data assumptions are marked LIVE / STALE / FREED-RESIDUE / UNOWNED by tracing provenance to a live root, swept transitively on a user retraction, compacted (the lesson survives, the directive dies), and tombstoned so the same garbage is not re-learned. The instruments are invoked directly; a fifth skill, the looper, runs them in order and logs each decision to a shared, user-editable log. A SessionStart memory override extends the built-in per-project memory system like a derived class — base read/write untouched, the shared VLDS store living in the project's .claude/vlds/ directory, the gate's storage tiers persisted as per-tier partition files whose expiry the gc owns. The collector guards three barriers — read, write, and dispatch, the last catching a message addressed twice or one a later message already freed. No VLDS operation waits for the user's word or asks permission — each runs when owed, announced before and reported after; only version control and the disposal of what the user authored keep the per-act word. Five hooks carry the mechanical half — SessionStart injects the contract, a digest of the index, and an owner-voice digest, and hands every judged store operation to one operator subagent per session — launched at the first moment, continued for a bounded number of moments, then relaunched — whose derivation is what the session acts on: at the first prompt it reads the hot files whole and pools them into one informed response scoped to the session's first task, which is what the session's context receives in place of the files; on a candidate row or an unknown short message it judges; when judged debt shows it scores what is cold and a script places it, while the close is a script applying the session's record; UserPromptSubmit stamps each message's dispatch row and runs the dispatch barrier's mechanical half (FRESH when no earlier row resembles the message, the candidate named otherwise, a known short command derived from the store's own adoption tokens), pours the dispatcher at a new session's first prompt, naming every session by its id and its chat title, and prints the last turn close's report; PreToolUse asks before a store-named file is written outside the store or a placeholder or guessed-ahead time is persisted; PostToolUse runs the structural check, the whole verdict when it changed and one line when it did not, whose [STRAY] class names a store-shaped file found outside the store; Stop runs the light normalize sweep (attach, expire, the logger's overflow) through the register's gates — and every hook output carries the clock. Portable; no dependency on the roboto instance.

plugins.name: verification-discipline
plugins.description: Verification Discipline (truth-on-a-timer) — a standalone, self-obeying framework for WHEN a stale-or-wrong prior must be re-checked before it drives an action. Half-life decay classes decide when a prior has expired; an independent cost gate fires when a cheap canonical oracle exists for a load-bearing claim; confidence is barred as an input; and an action-scoped layer-priority rule keeps a stale policy from suppressing the check (verification is never insubordination). Sixteen rules in three groups, three mottos, and the live failure case they were derived from. Companion to the vlds gate — the when-to-verify policy behind it, not a second gate. Standalone; no external plugin dependencies.

plugins.name: emission-discipline
plugins.description: Emission Discipline (prose-may-hedge-fences-execute) — a standalone, self-obeying framework for WHAT the model is licensed to RELEASE into a code fence, and thus into user-owned systems. Models the experienced integration defect as (correct form available in-model) × (release layer that never checks the emission against it) — knowledge–emission divergence — and gates on what is about to be released, never on how casual the request was: eight defect classes by transmission vector, twenty-one rules in seven groups (mid-stream, turn-boundary, standing, mandate/license, session, delivery form, ask), a resident trigger table, a PreToolUse fence gate that asks before a persisted fence carries a hedged literal, a deployment residency map, and the two live case studies it was derived from and amended against. Consequential-side twin of verification-discipline: that framework gates what the model believes, this one gates what it releases. Ships the doctrine as a direct-invoke skill plus a resident-gate wrapper skill for user-level installs. Standalone; no external plugin dependencies.

plugins.name: src-fragger
plugins.description: src-fragger (frags-outlive-the-session) — every piece of code the agent writes to complete a task, anything that replaces manual, user-involved labor with a script the agent builds and runs and whose job no single tool call does (an edit, an append, a whole-file write, or one shell command is the tool's own call, never a frag; a script that does the tool's job because a heredoc failed on the text is the call in costume), is a frag, and a frag is written to the VLDS store's src/ directory and registered in src/frags.md, never to a scratchpad or a temp directory. The split is by worth, not by file type: the project's .claude/scratchpad/ is the always-git-ignored notebook (notes, plans, commit messages, logs, captured output, downloads kept for reading — the SessionStart hook seeds a .gitignore of * inside it, so it ignores itself whatever the project's own rules say), and .claude/vlds/src/ is the git-tracked home of every reusable and worthwhile output of that work, code or not: the frags in the task's directory, registered, and what they read or produced that is worth keeping — a fetched spec, a captured page, a downloaded source, a design spec, a run's report — in the task's out/ (src/<task>/out/), tracked and unregistered; a notebook file that turns out to be worth keeping — one a later task runs, reads or edits, or a commit is about to carry — graduates to src/ (code) or the task's out/ (anything else), a log a claim cites stays a note (the claim's entry carries what was read; the instrument that produced it is the output), nothing in the notebook is force-added to git, and a truly throwaway probe may stay there after the gate's ask. The harness scratchpad dies with the session and the notebook lives on one disk; a frag outlives both, so the next task updates it instead of rewriting it, the user can read and edit it (an edit is a ruling), and when the harness refuses the agent's own execution the frag is already where the user can run it — and before any hand-off the agent double-checks that the frag is registered, that the refusal survives a retry of the same call in a fresh tool call (a refusal is bound to the conversation's content — a fresh call or a fresh conversation can pass where a resume does not), that the user's word already covers the act, and that the interruption is a decision rather than labor. A SessionStart hook injects the contract, seeds the register and the notebook's .gitignore, says in one line when the project's root rules ignore src/ itself (never editing them), and in one more when src/ holds code the register does not name or the register names a path that is gone and not retired; a PreToolUse gate asks before a code file — by extension, a page included, or by a name such as CMakeLists.txt — is written to a temp location or to any project's .claude/scratchpad/. Shares the VLDS store; no other dependency.

plugins.name: envelope-discipline
plugins.description: Envelope Discipline (futures-land-as-fields) — a standalone, self-obeying framework for HOW a seam's configurables are shaped at the moment the seam is minted. Models interface calcification as (first-of-family mistaken for the whole story) × (no envelope reserved at the only cheap moment) and gates on what is about to be MINTED: the first option reveals the family and gets one named options envelope at birth; defaults are the null ask so no default carries doctrine; futures land as new named fields, never as signature breaks or per-knob rulings; the shape spans every layer of the seam, wire grammar included. Twelve rules in three groups, three mottos, and the live minting failure they were derived from. Shape-side sibling of verification-discipline (what may be believed) and emission-discipline (what may be released): this framework gates the contracts the other two operate across. Standalone; no external plugin dependencies.
